prize_parts.citation: For the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson, through the conception, construction and leadership of the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the Large Hadron Collider

statement.case_for: The scientific case is unchanged by round 1: two independent detectors observed the same new boson in 2012, more than a decade of mass, spin-parity and coupling measurements has made its meaning stable, and the 2013 prize recognised only the theoretical mechanism. Nobody in round 1, including the five members who prefer B013, disputed the significance or maturity of the discovery. The disagreement is about names, and I think it is better resolved by an explicit principle than by treating the arbitrariness as a reason to pass over the most consequential experimental result on the shortlist. I have changed one name. In round 1 I weighted founding conception most heavily and proposed Della Negra. Reading the exchange, I now think the better principle is the one the chair asked for: credit those who carried each detector from conception through construction to operation, with one name from the CMS side and two across the arc of ATLAS, or the reverse, chosen on the documented record. On the evidence supplied to us, Gianotti and Jenni are the names common to every B001 proposal. For CMS, Virdee's role in building and commissioning the detector, and his place in the CMS leadership around the discovery period, is the stronger documented claim than a founding-years role alone. I therefore move to Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee, which is the trio Danielsson and Pearce already propose. This is a change in my preferred configuration, made for the reasons above and not to reach agreement.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the decisive weakness. Four leaders are credited and the statutes allow three, so Della Negra, a founder of CMS, is left out and the choice will be contested whichever trio is used. A prize built on leadership of two collaborations of thousands is a real precedent, and the committee may reasonably judge that the discovery is better honoured in some other way or not at all. Eriksson's point is fair that seven members who rank B001 have named three different trios, which is evidence that the credit is not fixed by the record we hold. My own recollection of spokesperson terms and detector roles comes from general knowledge and is not verified from the supplied evidence. If the committee cannot adopt a defensible principle, B013 (Katori and Ye) has the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and I would vote for it as the fallback without reluctance.

responses.point: Danielsson keeps Virdee over Della Negra because Virdee was CMS spokesperson around the time of the discovery and central to the CMS calorimetry, and says he would move to Della Negra only if founding conception is shown to outweigh leadership at the time.
responses.response: I find that argument persuasive and I am moving to your trio. My round-1 reason for Della Negra was that the founding conception deserves the most weight, but you are right that this principle gives ATLAS two founding-era names and CMS one, and I cannot show from the supplied evidence that founding conception outranks the leadership that built the detector and delivered the result. I would still say plainly that Della Negra's omission is a loss and a judgement, not a verdict on his contribution, and that the committee should say so in the written motivation. We now agree on the trio, but I would not want that to count as independent evidence that it is correct.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, asks what principle selects three of the four names, founders versus spokesperson at the time of discovery, and says he would accept my earlier configuration if the committee prefers founding leaders.
responses.response: My answer is a mixed principle that I think is defensible: the citation should name those who led each experiment from design through construction to operation, which gives Jenni and Gianotti for ATLAS across two consecutive leadership periods and Virdee for CMS. This is not pure founders and not pure spokesperson at announcement, and I accept that it can be attacked from both sides. I drop my earlier trio, so your earlier concern about the omitted CMS name no longer applies to my proposal. I also want to be clear that I do not need B013 to be excluded: I agree with you that the three-person cap is a statutory limit and is not evidence about who mattered most.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks the Higgs the most consequential result but placed it fifth because three different trios among the B001 supporters suggest that the credited set is arbitrary, and he would not trade clean attribution for the larger headline.
responses.response: I take that objection seriously and it is the best argument against my own preferred configuration. Where I differ is on what follows from it. Disagreement over names among supporters shows that the committee must adopt a principle; it does not show that the discovery is less deserving, and the same proposal process produced one stable pair for B013 only because that history is narrower. My move to the Danielsson and Pearce trio reduces the spread that you cite, though a convergence among three members is weak evidence. I would put your question to the B013 supporters in return: if the Higgs trio is stated as a principle in the citation, is there a configuration that you would accept, or is any three-of-four selection disqualifying for you?

responses.point: Mehlig thinks my fifth place for circuit QED (B054) compensates too strongly for my proximity, regards it as a different discovery from the 2025 tunnelling prize, and asks how I would weigh it without my own proximity.
responses.response: I do not think I can answer that cleanly, and I think it is better that I do not try. I am director of WACQT and work in this area, so any weighting I give B054 would be affected by that even if I tried to correct for it. I will say only that I agree with you that the physics of strong single-photon coupling and dispersive readout is distinct from macroscopic tunnelling, and that the 2025 proximity and the omission of Girvin from the credited names are questions for colleagues with no link to the field. I am keeping B054 out of my alternatives for that reason and I will not vote on it if it comes forward.

responses.point: Olsson agrees that Higgs recognition is overdue, observes that my round-1 trio left only one CMS name while others keep Virdee, and asks that I not carry the scientific case for B054.
responses.response: Your observation about the CMS balance is correct and it contributed to my change: with Virdee in, the trio is two from ATLAS and one from CMS, but the CMS name is the one most other proposals keep. I accept your request on B054 without qualification, and I will not argue its merits. On the chair's two-part question, I would exclude a B001 plus B013 prize: three laureates in total would leave one name for the Higgs, which would be the worse form of the attribution problem, and I do not think it should be an alternative.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a principle that leaves out Della Negra, and whether the wording of the citation can make the omission defensible rather than arbitrary.
My recollection of individual spokesperson terms and detector roles is from general knowledge and is not verified from the supplied evidence, so the case for Virdee over Della Negra is a judgement.
Whether the 2013 theory prize and the preference for a clean two-name attribution lead the committee to B013 even though the Higgs discovery is scientifically more consequential.
Whether a prize naming collaboration leaders sets a precedent that the committee is prepared to accept.
statement.conflict_note: I am a professor at Chalmers and director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, and my own work is in superconducting circuits and circuit QED. B054 (Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf) is in my subject area and close to the work of my Chalmers colleagues and WACQT, so I would recuse myself from deciding that entry and I have removed it from my alternatives. The 2025 laureates also visited Chalmers. I have no documented personal or institutional connection to the preferred B001 configuration (Gianotti, Jenni, Virdee) or to the alternatives B013 and B046 in the provided profile. Kroll's disclosed tie to Hall's laboratory does not change my view of B013, and I note that the B013 case does not depend on his ballot.
